package_info.package_versions: All versions prior to 5.3.18 and 5.2.20 (also affects Spring Boot prior to 2.6.6)
package_info.why_malicious: The package contains a critical remote code execution (RCE) vulnerability (CVE-2022-22965, 'Spring4Shell') that allows attackers to exploit Java Reflection and DataBinder functionality to load arbitrary classes and execute attacker-supplied code on affected systems. This is a macro-level design flaw, not an intentionally malicious package, but the result is equivalent to a supply chain compromise due to the ease of exploitation.

execution_context.file_location: org.springframework.beans (DataBinder class, invoked during HTTP request deserialization)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code processes HTTP request parameters that manipulate internal Java class properties via reflection, allowing an attacker to write a web shell or execute arbitrary commands on the server.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The ability to set internal class properties via HTTP parameters is highly abnormal and enables attackers to control application behavior and execute arbitrary code.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal HTTP request processing should not allow modification of internal Java classloader or pipeline properties. This behavior violates the principle of least privilege and safe deserialization.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate use of DataBinder is to bind simple form data to POJOs, not to internal server or classloader properties.
key_indicators: Manipulation of classloader or pipeline properties via HTTP parameters
Ability to write files or execute commands from user-supplied input
Use of reflection to access non-public fields

execution_context.trigger: runtime (HTTP request with command injection payload)
execution_context.file_location: Injected web shell or JSP file written to webroot via manipulated pipeline properties

malicious_snippets.code_language: jsp (Java Server Pages, executed by Tomcat)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the attacker sends a request to a maliciously written JSP web shell, which executes the supplied command (e.g., launching the calculator application) on the server.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The presence of a writable web shell in the webroot and the ability to execute arbitrary system commands via HTTP requests is a hallmark of RCE exploitation.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal web applications should not allow arbitrary file writes to the webroot or execution of system commands from user input.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: JSP files are used for dynamic web content, but should not be writable or executable by untrusted users.
key_indicators: Web shell file written to webroot
Execution of system commands via HTTP parameters
Unexpected new JSP files appearing in deployed applications

attack_chain.action: Attacker sends a crafted HTTP request with malicious parameters targeting DataBinder reflection vulnerability.
attack_chain.leads_to: Allows attacker to modify internal server properties and write a web shell to the webroot.

attack_chain.action: Attacker accesses the maliciously written JSP web shell and sends commands for execution.
attack_chain.leads_to: Remote code execution on the server, full system compromise.

behavioral_signatures: HTTP requests containing suspicious parameters targeting classloader or pipeline properties
Unexpected file writes to webroot directories (e.g., new .jsp files)
Execution of system commands from web application context
file_indicators: New or modified .jsp files in webroot (e.g., /stupidRumor_war_exploded/fuck.jsp)
Files with names or content indicative of web shells
network_indicators: Inbound HTTP requests with parameters like class.module.classLoader.resources.context.parent.pipeline.first.pattern
Outbound connections or callbacks initiated by web shells
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor HTTP request logs for suspicious parameters targeting internal Java class properties. Watch for new or modified .jsp files in web application directories. Alert on execution of system commands from the web application process. Use file integrity monitoring and web application firewalls to detect exploitation attempts.
